## Benchmarking PINNs, PIKANs and finite-difference methods for option pricing

I compared Crank–Nicolson, Physics-Informed Neural Networks
(PINNs) and Physics-Informed Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks
(PIKANs), using the analytical Black–Scholes solution as
a reference.

The evaluation considers accuracy, runtime, convergence and
sensitivity to volatility.

In the tested one-dimensional setting, Crank–Nicolson provided
the strongest combination of accuracy and computational efficiency.

## The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus for Absolutely Continuous Functions

My undergraduate dissertation at the University of Galway
examined how absolute continuity connects differentiation
and integration.

The central question is when a function can be recovered
by integrating its derivative. Absolute continuity provides
the appropriate framework for this form of the Fundamental
Theorem of Calculus.

This expository project developed my experience in rigorous
mathematical reasoning and communicating a sustained
mathematical argument.
